blocks: Same lean Person hub, plus a garden pointer and interest areas. Precedent: Person/Maggie Appleton, Person/Mischa van den Burg, Person/Nikita Voloboev, Person/Simon Spati, Person/Devine Lu Linvega, Person/Nicole van der Hoeven, Person/John Mavrick, Person/Lyz.

In this garden, the Maker entities model a real person by what they make: music, music theory, music technology or art. Each kind of thing a person makes has its own child entity, and the rules on this page apply to every child.
Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Theory — Music Theorist, a maker of theory whose field is music
Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Tech — Music Technologist, a maker of technology whose field is music
Each child page says what counts as its instance, the cases near its boundary, and any frontmatter of its own. Everything else is on this page.
A Logseq/Entity/Person hub for someone whose making, in a field a child entity covers, is a significant part of their public identity and of what the garden records about them.

Making means producing the work: composing, performing, producing, writing theory, building instruments or software, making art. A person who shares, curates, teaches, broadcasts or writes about other people's work, and makes none of their own, stays a Person.
Writing, architecture, design and software outside music are fields the family does not cover yet. A person who makes things only in those fields stays a Person.
Not an instance: a band or ensemble, a work, a recording, or a fictional Logseq/Entity/Person/Character.

A page carries only the most specific maker entities that fit, and may carry several from any field. Every maker entity is a kind of person, so the page leaves Logseq/Entity/Person out of logseq-entity::. A page marked Songwriter leaves out Composer and Musician.

Logseq/Entity/Person/Knowledge Gardener still asks for Person first. A maker who keeps a public garden lists the maker entities, then Knowledge Gardener, and leaves Person out, until codekiln decides whether Knowledge Gardener follows Logseq/Entity/Hierarchy/Discussion/Analysis/Opus/26/10/01/0611 ET Mark each page with the most specific entity in each lineage.
No page lists Maker itself in logseq-entity::. Each maker's hub lists the child entity for what they make.
The entity for what the person is best known for making comes first.
Person/Madonna writes songs and performs them:
Jean-Philippe Rameau composed operas and wrote the theory of functional harmony:
A person known to make music in an unknown role carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music. A person known to make art in an unknown form carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Art.

Music Theorist and Music Technologist name makers of theory and technology, who are Musicians only when the page also carries Musician or one of its kinds. Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music shows the marking for a technologist who also makes music in an unknown role.

A page for something a maker made points back to the maker's hub with created-by::, as software project and book pages in the garden already do. A published stage or project identity is represented separately by Logseq/Entity/Identity; Logseq/Frontmatter/created-by-identities records that identity's credit on the creation. The maker's linked references then list their works, so the hub needs no hand-kept list of them.
A work with several makers lists the hub of each maker that has one in created-by::, comma-separated.

The lean hub from Logseq/Entity/Person, with one line near the top saying what the person makes. Person/John Adams reads "American composer and conductor." under ## About. A new hub puts the line under ## About. On an older hub, a line under ## Bio, #Bio or #Bio/Short serves. Whoever marks a hub that has no such line, such as Person/Stephen Marotto, adds ## About with the line.
Naming, aliases and deduplication follow Logseq/Entity/Person.

In this garden, Artist pages model a real person who makes works of art: painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, installation, video, performance art or sound art. An Artist is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker, and the rest follows that page.
A person whose artworks are a significant part of their public identity.
A page carries Artist itself when the art form is not sound or is unknown. An artist whose material is sound carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Art/Sound in place of Artist.
Architecture, design and typeface design are fields the family does not cover yet.
A creative coder who makes visual art carries Artist. A creative coder who also makes music adds Musician or the kind of Musician that names their role.
Album covers and stage visuals made as part of a music career count when the garden records them as artworks.
An artwork page has created-by:: linking the artist's hub, as Art/Work/The Sudarium of Saint Veronica links the engraver Claude Mellan.

In this garden, Sound Artist pages model a real person who makes art whose material is sound, presented as art: sound installations, sound sculptures, soundwalks, and site-specific or gallery works with sound. A Sound Artist is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Art, so a page marked Sound Artist leaves Artist out.
A person whose sound art is a significant part of their public identity: Person/George Rhoads and his audiokinetic sculptures, Person/Courtney Brown.

A sound artist who also writes concert pieces, or fixed-media works presented as compositions, adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition: Person/Wei Yang. One who releases tracks as an electronic producer adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Production.
A sound artist who performs their work live carries Sound Artist and Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance: Person/Huichun Yang.
A sound artist who also makes music in an unknown role carries Sound Artist and Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music: Person/Ranger Liu, Person/Tom Whiston.

Why each segment under Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker names what the person makes, why Songwriter and Conductor nest under Composer and Performer, why the shared rules sit on Maker, and what the family replaced.
Each entity name under Maker says what the person makes

Maker/Music/Theory names a maker of theory whose field is music. Heinrich Glarean is known for his theory, including his naming of the Ionian and Aeolian modes, so his hub carries Music Theorist alone, without Musician. Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Tech works the same way for a person who builds a synthesis method or a music programming language.
Each entity name under Maker says what the person makes

Theory and Tech nest under Music because music is their field, so the music entities stay together in one namespace. They are kinds of Maker. Composer, Performer and Music Producer are kinds of Musician.
Each entity name under Maker says what the person makes

A person who builds music software and also makes music carries both entities, as logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Tech]], [[Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music]] does for a technologist whose role in music is unknown. Neither entity implies the other, so the page lists two lineages.
Each entity name under Maker says what the person makes
The alternative was to make Theory and Tech kinds of Musician. That would mark Glarean as a musician, and would leave no way to mark a technologist who makes no music.
Each entity name under Maker says what the person makes
Songwriter and Conductor nest under Composer and Performer

Writing a song is composing, and conducting is performing through an ensemble. Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition/Song is a kind of Composer, and Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance/Conducting is a kind of Performer.
Songwriter and Conductor nest under Composer and Performer

With each page marked by the most specific entity in each lineage, as Logseq/Entity/Hierarchy/Discussion/Analysis/Opus/26/10/01/0611 ET Mark each page with the most specific entity in each lineage recommends, Person/Madonna carries Songwriter and Performer, and Songwriter already says she composes.
Songwriter and Conductor nest under Composer and Performer

The alternative was to put Song and Conducting directly under Music, beside Composition and Performance. A songwriter's page would then need Composer as well to say that songs are compositions, or the Composer namespace would leave songwriters out.
Songwriter and Conductor nest under Composer and Performer

Marking, created-by:: on works, the lean hub with one line saying what the person makes, and the marking for an unknown role are the same for every maker. They are written once, on Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker, following My/Principle/Simplify/Don't Repeat Yourself DRY. Each child page holds only what differs: what counts as its instance, the cases near its boundary, and any frontmatter of its own.
The alternative was to repeat the shared rules on every child page. A change to one rule would then need an edit on each child page, and the copies would disagree whenever one was missed.
The other shape put the music entities under Logseq/Entity/Person/Music, with Person/Music/Composition, Person/Music/Theory and the rest beneath it.

That shape has no common parent for music and art. A sound artist and a composer share the marking, created-by:: and hub rules, which would either sit on Logseq/Entity/Person, where they would apply to every person, or be copied into Person/Music and a separate Person/Art.
Person/Music also names a field without saying what the person does in it. Maker says that every entity in the family is about making something, and the segments under it say what is made.
2026-09-27 Sun — Logseq/Entity/Person/Musician added, for people whose work includes making, performing or producing music. Each hub that carried it listed Logseq/Entity/Person as well.

2026-10-10 Sat — codekiln renamed Musician to Logseq/Entity/Person/Music/ian in the morning, and later that day to Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music, rewriting it as the parent of the music maker entities and adding Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker and its children. Both old names stay as aliases of the Musician page.
In this garden, Musician pages model a real person who makes music: who composes it, performs it or produces it. Marking, works and hub shape follow Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker.
A person who makes music in any role, when making music is a significant part of their public identity and of what the garden records about them.

A page carries this entity itself only when the person's role in music is unknown: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music]]. When the role is known, the page carries the child entity for it.

A music teacher, critic, historian, broadcaster, curator or label owner who makes no music leaves Musician out. One who published theory, a theory textbook or a teaching method carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Theory, as Guido of Arezzo does for his solmization syllables. Everyone else in this list stays a Logseq/Entity/Person.

A Music Theorist or Music Technologist is a Musician only when the page also carries Musician or one of its kinds. A technologist who also makes music in an unknown role carries both: logseq-entity:: [[Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Tech]], [[Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music]].

A stage or project name with its own release identity has a separate Logseq/Entity/Identity/Music page linked to the person through Logseq/Entity/Identity/Frontmatter/identity-of. The published name is the identity page title, so it appears directly in autocomplete.

A band with its own identity follows Logseq/Entity/Identity/Music/Band and has a page separate from its members' hubs. Existing solo aliases and group pages remain valid until deliberately separated or renamed.

In this garden, Composer pages model a real person who writes music as works: pieces, scores, soundtracks, and fixed-media or electroacoustic works. A Composer is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music, and the rest follows Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker.
A person whose composed works are a significant part of their public identity, in any tradition: concert music, jazz, film and game music, acousmatic, electroacoustic and computer music.
A fixed-media or tape piece is a composed work, so its maker is a Composer: Person/Pierre Henry, Person/Eliane Radigue.

A person known mainly for songs in the popular, folk, blues or rock traditions carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition/Song and leaves Composer out, since a Songwriter is a kind of Composer. Franz Schubert, who wrote art songs, and Tito Puente, who wrote tunes for his band, carry Composer.
An improviser whose music exists only in performance carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance. An improviser who also writes pieces carries Composer as well.

An electronic producer who releases tracks carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Production, and adds Composer for works presented as compositions, such as concert pieces or film scores: Person/Daniel Lopatin.
A person who makes sound installations or sound sculptures carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Art/Sound, and adds Composer when they also write pieces for concert or release: Person/Wei Yang.

A composer who also writes music theory adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Theory; one who also leads ensembles from the podium adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance/Conducting, as Person/John Adams does.

A composed work follows Logseq/Entity/Music/Work for placement under its credited identity or the composer's hub, with created-by:: linking the known composer and Logseq/Frontmatter/created-by-identities preserving a separate published identity when applicable.
Person/Steve Reich, Person/John Adams, Person/Iannis Xenakis

In this garden, Songwriter pages model a real person who writes songs: the music, the words, or both. A Songwriter is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition, so a page marked Songwriter leaves Composer out.
A person known mainly for songs in the popular, folk, blues or rock traditions, including lyricists: Person/Madonna, W. C. Handy.

A composer of art songs, such as Franz Schubert and his Lieder, carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition. So does a jazz or Latin bandleader who writes tunes for the band, such as Tito Puente and "Oye Como Va".
A songwriter who also writes other kinds of works, such as concert pieces or film scores, still carries Songwriter alone. The hub's line saying what the person makes names the other works.
A singer-songwriter carries Songwriter and Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance: Person/Madonna, Person/Adrianne Lenker.
A singer who performs songs other people wrote carries Performance only.
A producer who shapes a song in the studio without writing it carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Production.
A song is a Logseq/Entity/Music/Work, filed under the songwriter's hub as Composer works are.

In this garden, Performer pages model a real person who performs music for listeners: who plays an instrument, sings, improvises, DJs or live-codes. A Performer is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music, and the rest follows Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker.
A person whose public performing is a significant part of their identity: soloists, ensemble and orchestra players, singers, bandleaders who play in their band, improvisers, DJs and live coders.
The hub's line saying what the person makes names the instrument or voice, as "violinist" or "pipa player".
A teacher of an instrument who does not perform in public stays a Logseq/Entity/Person.
A person who leads an ensemble from the podium carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance/Conducting in place of Performer.

A live coder performs by writing code in front of an audience, and carries Performer: Person/Atsushi Tadokoro. A live coder who also builds the language or software that live coders perform with adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Tech.

A performer who writes the pieces they play adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition. One known mainly for songs in the popular, folk, blues or rock traditions adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition/Song, as Person/Adrianne Lenker does.
A sound artist whose work is performed live, such as a breath or object performance in a gallery, carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Art/Sound and Performer.

A performance page links its performers with performer::, as Logseq/Entity/Music/Performance and Logseq/Entity/Music/Recording describe, and those links list the performances in the performer's linked references.

In this garden, Conductor pages model a real person who leads an orchestra, choir or other ensemble as its conductor. A Conductor is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance, so a page marked Conductor leaves Performer out.
A person whose conducting is a significant part of their public identity: orchestral and choral conductors and music directors.
A conductor who also plays an instrument in public still carries Conductor alone. The hub's line saying what the person makes names the instrument.
A bandleader who plays in the band carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance.
A composer who conducts carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition and Conductor: Person/John Adams, Person/Guy Reibel.

In this garden, Music Producer pages model a real person who makes recorded music: who produces, records, mixes or masters recordings, or makes tracks as an electronic producer. A Music Producer is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music, and the rest follows Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker.
Record producers, recording and mixing engineers, and electronic producers who release their own tracks: Person/Eduardo Ramos.
An electronic producer who also writes works presented as compositions, such as concert pieces or film scores, adds Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition: Person/Daniel Lopatin.
A DJ who plays sets carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance, and adds Music Producer when they release tracks of their own.
A person who builds the plugins, devices or software that producers use carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Tech.
A release follows Logseq/Entity/Music/Recording: it lives under the credited Logseq/Entity/Identity/Music when represented separately, or under the producer's hub otherwise.

In this garden, Music Technologist pages model a real person who makes technology for music: instruments, synthesis methods, music software and programming languages, plugins and devices, and the hardware or firmware music runs on. A Music Technologist is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker whose field is music, and the rest follows that page.

A person whose music technology is a significant part of their public identity: the author of a music programming language (Person/James McCartney and SuperCollider), the inventor of a synthesis method (Person/John Chowning and FM synthesis), or a developer of tools for a music application (Person/Leo Bernard).
Instrument builders count, from acoustic instruments to synthesizers.
A Music Technologist is a maker of technology. A person who also makes music carries the kind of Musician that names their role as well, or Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music when the role is unknown.

A person who programs patches or builds systems only for their own pieces leaves Music Technologist out: Person/Huichun Yang carries Sound Artist and Performer, and Person/Wei Yang carries Sound Artist and Composer. Music Technologist is for technology other musicians use: a language, a synthesis method, or a plugin, device or instrument other people play, such as Person/Tobias Hunke's Max for Live devices.
A live coder who also builds the language or software live coders perform with carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Performance and Music Technologist.
A researcher who publishes about music technology without building it carries only the entities for what else they make, or stays a Logseq/Entity/Person.
A software project, device or instrument the person made has its own page with created-by:: linking the hub. Software follows Logseq/Entity/Software/Project.

In this garden, Music Theorist pages model a real person who makes music theory: treatises, systems of scales, modes or harmony, methods of analysis, and theory textbooks. A Music Theorist is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker whose field is music, and the rest follows that page.
A person whose theory is a significant part of their public identity, whether or not they made music: a theorist who named the modes or built a system of parent scales counts.

A Music Theorist is a maker of theory. A person who also made music carries the kind of Musician that names their role as well, as a composer-theorist carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Composition and Music Theorist.

A teacher whose published textbook or teaching method sets out how music is organized counts. A teacher who has published no theory, method or textbook carries only the entities for what else they make, or stays a Logseq/Entity/Person.

A music historian, critic or ethnomusicologist writes about music, and carries only the entities for what else they make. Collecting folk songs in the field is research of this kind: a composer who collected folk songs carries Composer and leaves out Music Theorist.
A researcher who invents a synthesis method or builds music software carries Logseq/Entity/Person/Maker/Music/Tech.

For scales, Music Theorist is for a person who names or classifies them in writing, as Heinrich Glarean named the Ionian and Aeolian modes. A composer who builds their music on a scale or tuning carries the entities for their music: Yatsuhashi Kengyō, who is credited with the hirajōshi koto tuning and played the koto, carries Composer and Performer, and Claude Debussy, who built pieces on the whole-tone scale, carries Composer.
A treatise or textbook has a book page with created-by:: linking the theorist's hub.
In this garden, Professor pages model real people who hold or held a university professorial appointment, including emeritus professors.
A Professor is a kind of Logseq/Entity/Person, using the same Person/Full Name hub and deduplication rules. An appointment adds academic context to the person's existing hub.
The hub carries Professor as its most specific entity in this lineage, omitting the broader Person marker. Independent entities from other lineages may appear alongside Professor when applicable.

A doctorate, book authorship, research position, guest lecture, or course contribution alone does not establish a professorship. University faculty biographies, appointment notices, and curriculum vitae establish the appointment and its dates.
academic-title:: records the current named professorship or emeritus title as plain text when known.
university-affiliation:: links the current university when it already exists in the graph; an official university link in the body can identify an institution without a graph page.
The Academic Appointment section distinguishes the university, school or department, and appointment title. Joint appointments retain each school or department.
The Previous Appointments section records former universities and roles with dates where established. Historical appointments remain dated in the body rather than appearing as current affiliations.
Sources retain the date of an appointment notice or curriculum vitae when it matters to interpreting a career history. An old biography does not establish a current affiliation.
About states the person's research field and the questions their scholarship addresses. Education may record degrees and universities when useful.

A separately modeled publication uses its own entity, such as Logseq/Entity/Book or Logseq/Entity/Article, with created-by:: pointing to every credited author who has a person hub. The person's linked references collect those publications.

Selected Publications gives context for significant works rather than reproducing a complete bibliography. A publication without a garden page may appear as a descriptive external link with its title, venue, and publication year. An official publication list can supply the complete bibliography.
Book and article entity definitions govern publication titles, dates, and coauthor credits; a publication is not a child Professor instance merely because it sits under a person's namespace.

A Logseq/Entity/Course page identifies its instructor through instructor::; the professor's linked references collect the courses. A Teaching section may explain a course's relationship to the professor's research.
A Logseq/Entity/Course/Syllabus page records a particular offering's curriculum. Reading, citation, case authorship, and guest participation do not establish an instructor appointment.

The person hub opens with the person's name, preferably linked to an official faculty biography, followed by About. Appointment, career, research, publication, education, and teaching sections appear where substantive information is available.
Faculty biographies, official publication records, and curriculum vitae support academic facts. Shared property conventions live on Logseq/Frontmatter.
In this garden, Podcast pages model a recurring show: a feed of episodes published under one title by one or more hosts.
A show with its own title and feed, such as Hard Fork/Pod or Person/Nathaniel Whittemore/Pod. The show is what someone subscribes to; an episode is what someone listens to.
Not a Podcast: a single episode, which is a Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode; the host's or a guest's Logseq/Entity/Person hub; the network or company that publishes several shows.
Each episode gets its own Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode page and belongs to one show.
A show's page carries Logseq/Entity/Podcast, and each episode's page carries Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode.
Episode pages file beneath the show page's namespace, so Logseq's namespace listing on the show page lists the episodes the garden holds.
The show page is the Pod namespace its episodes file under:
Person/<Host>/Pod for a show led by a host who has a person page, as with Person/Nathaniel Whittemore/Pod.
The show page is the Pod namespace its episodes file under:
<Show>/Pod for a show known by its own name or with several hosts, as with Hard Fork/Pod and Latent Space/Pod.
The show page is the Pod namespace its episodes file under:
alias:: carries the show's published title, its Podcast/<Show Name> form, and any short form likely to be searched.
Some show pages and episodes were filed with a Podcast segment, as with People I (Mostly) Admire/Podcast. Prefer Pod for new pages and leave existing ones as filed unless a migration is asked for.
Search in order: the show's home or feed URL; the show title and its aliases; */Pod and */Podcast pages; the host's person namespace. Classify as existing, similar, new, or blocked.
One page per show. A show page is created when the garden holds more than one of its episodes, or when the author asks for one.
Set created-by:: to the host's person page, or to each host's page when the show has several.
Optional: date-created:: for the date the show launched, when known.
Shared frontmatter conventions live on Logseq/Frontmatter.
The first body block is an H1 linking the show's home page: - # [Show Title](https://example.com/show).
A line or two under the H1 names the hosts and what the show covers.
Optional ## Links for the feed, the show's YouTube channel, and its page.
Episode notes stay on the episode pages. The show page holds what is true of every episode: the hosts, the subject, the publishing schedule, where to listen.
Logseq/Entity/Podcast/Episode — one episode of the show. The Podcast Episode definition page covers episode naming and page shape, including episodes that are also YouTube videos.
Logseq/Entity/Person — the hosts. A host's person hub links to the show page.
Logseq/Entity/Series — says how to name the page of an episode that belongs to a named sequence within the show.
In this garden, Podcast Episode pages model one episode of a Logseq/Entity/Podcast, captured as listening notes or a recording prepared for publication.
What counts as a Podcast Episode
One specific episode of a show, usually with a title, a host, an air date, and often a URL of its own.
What counts as a Podcast Episode

Not Podcast Episodes: the show itself, which is a Logseq/Entity/Podcast; the host's person hub; a guest's person hub; a Logseq/Entity/Quote pulled from an episode; a Logseq/Entity/Concept page that synthesizes ideas an episode discussed.
What counts as a Podcast Episode
An episode is part of one show. Its page carries the Episode marker, and the show's page carries the Podcast marker.
The episode page files under its show's namespace, and its created-by:: names the show's host.

Episode pages live under the show's Pod namespace, dated: Person/<Host>/Pod/<YY>/<MM> <Episode Title>, or <Show>/Pod/<YY>/<MM> <Episode Title> for a show filed under its own name. Logseq/Entity/Podcast says where the show page goes.
On disk that is pages/Person___<Host>___Pod___<YY>___<MM> <Episode Title>.md.
Episode pages live under the show's Pod namespace, dated: Person/<Host>/Pod/<YY>/<MM> <Episode Title>, or <Show>/Pod/<YY>/<MM> <Episode Title> for a show filed
